sections.title: Look Back (Review)
paragraphs: Joshua led the people across the Jordan River into the Promised Land. Each family was given part of the land as their inheritance just as God had promised to Abraham.

sections.title: Look Up (New Teaching)
paragraphs: After many years when Joshua was old, he called all the other leaders of the Israelites together. He said, "Today choose whom you will serve. But I and my household together will serve the LORD." The other leaders agreed with Joshua. They said, "We too will worship only the LORD, the Creator."

For only two generations, the Israelites kept their word and only worshiped God. The Bible teaches that after some time, the Israelites cried out to God’s prophet Samuel. They said, “Every other nation around has a king. Appoint a king for us so we will be like those other nations.” God said to Samuel, “The people have again rejected me as their King. Give the people what they are asking for but warn them that “the king will take your sons and daughters and make them work for him. He will take the best from the land. When that happens, you will cry out for relief from your king, but I will not answer you.” But the people still demanded a king.
Let’s read some verses from the Holy Scriptures, the Bible, that relate to this story.

These verses teach us that the human heart is restless — we keep reaching for things we can see and control, instead of trusting God. Israel did this when they demanded a king "like the other nations." And yet, even though they turned from God's way, God did not abandon them. He heard them, gave them what they asked, and stayed with them. God kept leading His people toward something better — a King who would never fail them. That King is Jesus Christ, who rules with grace and love.
What did you learn from these Scriptures?
Think a little — how will you practice what you have learned?

sections.title: Look Forward (Obedience)
paragraphs: Are you trusting anything else to provide the peace and security only God can give? Let’s ask God to help us trust him with our whole heart.
I hope you enjoyed this story. When can we meet again?
Do you think someone else should hear this story?
